backend, or using serverless functions.</p></div></header><h2 id="how-to-connect-to-your-postgres-databases" class="group scroll-mt-24">How to connect to your Postgres databases<a href="#how-to-connect-to-your-postgres-databases" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h2>
<p>How you connect to your database depends on where you're connecting from:</p>
<ul>
<li>For frontend applications, use the <a href="#data-apis-and-client-libraries" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Data API</a></li>
<li>For Postgres clients, use a connection string<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><strong>Use the <a href="#direct-connection" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">direct connection string</a> for single sessions or Postgres native commands</strong>. For example, database GUIs, client applications like <a href="https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/app-pgdump.html" aria-label="External Source: pg_dump" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">pg_dump<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-external-link inline-block align-[-1px] ml-0.5 text-lighter" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15 3h6v6"></path><path d="M10 14 21 3"></path><path d="M18 13v6a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H5a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V8a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h6"></path></svg></a>, <a href="/docs/guides/deployment/database-migrations" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">migrations</a>, <a href="/docs/guides/platform/migrating-within-supabase/backup-restore" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">backup-restore</a>, or specifying connections for <a href="/docs/guides/database/postgres/setup-replication-external" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">replication</a>. The direct endpoint is on IPv6, or on IPv4 if the project has the <a href="/docs/guides/platform/ipv4-address" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">IPv4 add-on</a>.</li>
<li><strong>Use <a href="#pooler-session-mode" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">pooler session mode</a></strong> for application traffic from persistent clients on IPv4-only networks,</li>
<li><strong>Use <a href="#pooler-transaction-mode" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">pooler transaction mode</a></strong> for application traffic from temporary clients (for example, serverless or edge functions).</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p>The table below summarizes each mode, its host and port, IP version support per project tier, and what it's best used for:</p>

<h2 id="data-apis-and-client-libraries" class="group scroll-mt-24">Data APIs and client libraries<a href="#data-apis-and-client-libraries" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h2>
<p>The Data APIs allow you to interact with your database using REST or GraphQL requests. You can use these APIs to fetch and insert data from the frontend, as long as you have <a href="/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">RLS</a> enabled.</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="/docs/guides/api" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">REST</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/guides/graphql/api" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">GraphQL</a></li>
</ul>
<p>For convenience, you can also use the <a href="/docs/reference" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Supabase client libraries</a>, which wrap the Data APIs with a developer-friendly interface and automatically handle authentication:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/introduction" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">JavaScript</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/reference/dart/introduction" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Flutter</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/reference/swift" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Swift</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/reference/python/introduction" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Python</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/reference/csharp/introduction" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">C#</a></li>
<li><a href="/docs/reference/kotlin/introduction" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Kotlin</a></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="direct-connection" class="group scroll-mt-24">Direct connection<a href="#direct-connection" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h2>
<p>The direct connection string connects directly to your Postgres instance. It is ideal for persistent servers, such as virtual machines (VMs) and long-lasting containers. Examples include AWS EC2 machines, Fly.io VMs, and DigitalOcean Droplets.</p>

<h2 id="poolers" class="group scroll-mt-24">Poolers<a href="#poolers" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h2>
<p>Supabase offers two poolers. The <strong>Shared Pooler</strong> (<a href="https://github.com/supabase/supavisor" aria-label="External Source: Supavisor" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Supavisor<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-external-link inline-block align-[-1px] ml-0.5 text-lighter" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15 3h6v6"></path><path d="M10 14 21 3"></path><path d="M18 13v6a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H5a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V8a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h6"></path></svg></a>) is multi-tenant, available on every project, and IPv4-only. The <strong>Dedicated Pooler</strong> (<a href="https://www.pgbouncer.org/" aria-label="External Source: PgBouncer" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">PgBouncer<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-external-link inline-block align-[-1px] ml-0.5 text-lighter" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15 3h6v6"></path><path d="M10 14 21 3"></path><path d="M18 13v6a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H5a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V8a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h6"></path></svg></a>) is available on paid plans and co-located with your Postgres instance; like the direct connection, it is on IPv6, or on IPv4 if the project has the <a href="/docs/guides/platform/ipv4-address" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">IPv4 add-on</a>.</p>
<h3 id="pooler-session-mode" class="group scroll-mt-24">Pooler session mode<a href="#pooler-session-mode" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>The session mode connection string connects to your Postgres instance via the Shared Pooler (Supavisor). This is only recommended as an alternative to a Direct Connection when connecting from an IPv4-only network.</p>
<p>The connection string looks like this:</p>

<h2 id="dedicated-pooler" class="group scroll-mt-24">Dedicated pooler<a href="#dedicated-pooler" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h2>
<p>For paying customers, we provision a Dedicated Pooler (<a href="https://www.pgbouncer.org/" aria-label="External Source: PgBouncer" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">PgBouncer<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-external-link inline-block align-[-1px] ml-0.5 text-lighter" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15 3h6v6"></path><path d="M10 14 21 3"></path><path d="M18 13v6a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H5a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V8a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h6"></path></svg></a>) that's co-located with your Postgres database. The Dedicated Pooler runs in transaction mode only - for session mode, use the <a href="#pooler-session-mode" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Shared Pooler</a>. It is reachable over IPv6, or over IPv4 if the project has the <a href="/docs/guides/platform/ipv4-address" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">IPv4 add-on</a>.</p>
<p>The connection string looks like this:</p>

<p>The Dedicated Pooler ensures best performance and latency, while using up more of your project's compute resources. If your network supports IPv6 or you have the IPv4 add-on, we encourage you to use the Dedicated Pooler over the Shared Pooler.</p>
<p>Get your project's Dedicated pooler connection string from your project dashboard by clicking <a href="/dashboard/project/_?showConnect=true&method=transaction" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Connect</a>.</p>
<h2 id="more-about-connection-pooling" class="group scroll-mt-24">More about connection pooling<a href="#more-about-connection-pooling" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h2>
<p>Connection pooling improves database performance by reusing existing connections between queries. This reduces the overhead of establishing connections and improves scalability.</p>
<p>You can use an application-side pooler or a server-side pooler (Supabase automatically provides one called Supavisor), depending on whether your backend is persistent or serverless.</p>
<h3 id="application-side-poolers" class="group scroll-mt-24">Application-side poolers<a href="#application-side-poolers" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>Application-side poolers are built into connection libraries and API servers, such as Prisma, SQLAlchemy, and PostgREST. They maintain several active connections with Postgres or a server-side pooler, reducing the overhead of establishing connections between queries. When deploying to static architecture, such as long-standing containers or VMs, application-side poolers are satisfactory on their own.</p>
<h3 id="server-side-poolers" class="group scroll-mt-24">Server-side poolers<a href="#server-side-poolers" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>Postgres connections are like a WebSocket. Once established, they are preserved until the client (application server) disconnects. A server might only make a single 10 ms query, but needlessly reserve its database connection for seconds or longer.</p>
<p>Server-side poolers, such as Supabase's <a href="https://github.com/supabase/supavisor" aria-label="External Source: Supavisor" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Supavisor<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-external-link inline-block align-[-1px] ml-0.5 text-lighter" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M15 3h6v6"></path><path d="M10 14 21 3"></path><path d="M18 13v6a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H5a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V8a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h6"></path></svg></a> in transaction mode, sit between clients and the database and can be thought of as load balancers for Postgres connections.</p>
<figure><img alt="New migration files trigger migrations on the preview instance." loading="lazy" width="1851" height="907" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="rounded-md w-full" style="color:transparent" srcset="/docs/_next/image?url=%2Fdocs%2Fimg%2Fguides%2Fdatabase%2Fconnecting-to-postgres%2Fhow-connection-pooling-works--light.png&w=1920&q=75 1x, /docs/_next/image?url=%2Fdocs%2Fimg%2Fguides%2Fdatabase%2Fconnecting-to-postgres%2Fhow-connection-pooling-works--light.png&w=3840&q=75 2x" src="/docs/_next/image?url=%2Fdocs%2Fimg%2Fguides%2Fdatabase%2Fconnecting-to-postgres%2Fhow-connection-pooling-works--light.png&w=3840&q=75"><figcaption class="text-center">Connecting to the database directly vs using a Connection Pooler</figcaption></figure>
<p>They maintain hot connections with the database and intelligently share them with clients only when needed, maximizing the amount of queries a single connection can service. They're best used to manage queries from auto-scaling systems, such as edge and serverless functions.</p>
<h2 id="connecting-with-ssl" class="group scroll-mt-24">Connecting with SSL<a href="#connecting-with-ssl" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h2>
<p>You should connect to your database using SSL wherever possible, to prevent snooping and man-in-the-middle attacks.</p>
<p>You can obtain your connection info and Server root certificate from your application's dashboard:</p>
<p><img src="/docs/img/database/database-settings-ssl.png" alt="Connection Info and Certificate."></p>

<h2 id="troubleshooting-and-postgres-connection-string-faqs" class="group scroll-mt-24">Troubleshooting and Postgres connection string FAQs<a href="#troubleshooting-and-postgres-connection-string-faqs" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h2>
<p>Below are answers to common challenges and queries.</p>
<h3 id="what-is-a-connection-refused-error" class="group scroll-mt-24">What is a “connection refused” error?<a href="#what-is-a-connection-refused-error" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>A “Connection refused” error typically means your database isn’t reachable. Ensure your Supabase project is running, confirm your database’s connection string, check firewall settings, and validate network permissions.</p>
<h3 id="what-is-the-fatal-password-authentication-failed-error" class="group scroll-mt-24">What is the “FATAL: Password authentication failed” error?<a href="#what-is-the-fatal-password-authentication-failed-error" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>This error occurs when your credentials are incorrect. Double-check your username and password from the Supabase dashboard. If the problem persists, reset your database password from the project settings.</p>
<h3 id="how-do-you-connect-using-ipv4" class="group scroll-mt-24">How do you connect using IPv4?<a href="#how-do-you-connect-using-ipv4" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>You have two options. The Shared Pooler (Supavisor) is IPv4-only on every project tier - use it in either session or transaction mode. Alternatively, add the <a href="/docs/guides/platform/ipv4-address" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">IPv4 add-on</a> to your project, which makes the direct connection and Dedicated Pooler reachable over IPv4 instead of IPv6.</p>
<h3 id="where-is-the-postgres-connection-string-in-supabase" class="group scroll-mt-24">Where is the Postgres connection string in Supabase?<a href="#where-is-the-postgres-connection-string-in-supabase" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>Your connection string is located in the Supabase Dashboard. Click the <a href="/dashboard/project/_?showConnect=true" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Connect</a> button at the top of the page.</p>
<h3 id="can-you-use-supavisor-and-pgbouncer-together" class="group scroll-mt-24">Can you use Supavisor and PgBouncer together?<a href="#can-you-use-supavisor-and-pgbouncer-together" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>You can technically use both, but it’s not recommended unless you’re specifically trying to increase the total number of concurrent client connections. In most cases, it is better to choose either PgBouncer or Supavisor for pooled or transaction-based traffic. Direct connections remain the best choice for long-lived sessions, and, if IPv4 is required for those sessions, Supavisor session mode can be used as an alternative. Running both poolers simultaneously increases the risk of hitting your database’s maximum connection limit on smaller compute tiers.</p>
<h3 id="how-does-the-default-pool-size-work" class="group scroll-mt-24">How does the default pool size work?<a href="#how-does-the-default-pool-size-work" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>Supavisor and PgBouncer work independently, but both reference the same pool size setting. For example, If you set the pool size to 30, Supavisor can open up to 30 server side connections to Postgres. These connections are shared between the session mode port (5432) and the transaction mode port (6543). Each mode can use up to 30 connections independently, or split them between both, but the total combined connections across both modes cannot exceed 30. PgBouncer can also open up to 30 connections under the same limit. If both poolers are active and reach their roles/modes limits at the same time, you could have as many as 60 backend connections hitting your database, in addition to any direct connections. You can adjust the pool size in <a href="/dashboard/project/_/database/settings" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Database settings</a> in the dashboard.</p>
<h3 id="what-is-the-difference-between-client-connections-and-backend-connections" class="group scroll-mt-24">What is the difference between client connections and backend connections?<a href="#what-is-the-difference-between-client-connections-and-backend-connections" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>There are two different limits to understand when working with poolers. The first is client connections, which refers to how many clients can connect to a pooler at the same time. This number is capped by your <a href="/docs/guides/platform/compute-and-disk#postgres-replication-slots-wal-senders-and-connections" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">compute tier’s “max pooler clients” limit</a>, and it applies independently to Supavisor and PgBouncer. The second is backend connections, which is the number of active connections a pooler opens to Postgres. This number is set by the pool size for that pooler.</p>

<h3 id="what-is-the-max-pooler-clients-limit" class="group scroll-mt-24">What is the max pooler clients limit?<a href="#what-is-the-max-pooler-clients-limit" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>The “max pooler clients” limit for your compute tier applies separately to Supavisor and PgBouncer. One pooler reaching its client limit does not affect the other. When a pooler reaches this limit, it stops accepting new client connections until existing ones are closed, but the other pooler remains unaffected. You can check your tier’s connection limits in the <a href="/docs/guides/platform/compute-and-disk#postgres-replication-slots-wal-senders-and-connections" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">compute and disk limits documentation</a>.</p>
<h3 id="where-can-you-see-current-connection-usage" class="group scroll-mt-24">Where can you see current connection usage?<a href="#where-can-you-see-current-connection-usage" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>You can track connection usage from the <a href="/dashboard/project/_/observability/database" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">Observability</a> section in your project dashboard. There are three key reports:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Database Connections:</strong> shows total active connections by role (this includes direct and pooled connections).</li>
<li><strong>Dedicated Pooler Client Connections:</strong> shows the number of active client connections to PgBouncer.</li>
<li><strong>Shared Pooler (Supavisor) Client Connections:</strong> shows the number of active client connections to Supavisor.</li>
</ul>
<p>Keep in mind that the Roles page is not real-time, it shows the connection count from the last refresh. If you need up-to-the-second data, set up Grafana or run the query against <code>pg_stat_activity</code> directly in SQL Editor. We have a few helpful queries for checking connections.</p>

<h3 id="why-are-there-active-connections-when-the-app-is-idle" class="group scroll-mt-24">Why are there active connections when the app is idle?<a href="#why-are-there-active-connections-when-the-app-is-idle" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>Even if your application isn’t making queries, some Supabase services keep persistent connections to your database. For example, Storage, PostgREST, and our health checker all maintain long-lived connections. You usually see a small baseline of active connections from these services.</p>
<h3 id="why-do-connection-strings-have-different-ports" class="group scroll-mt-24">Why do connection strings have different ports?<a href="#why-do-connection-strings-have-different-ports" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>Different modes use different ports:</p>
<ul>
<li>Direct connection: <code>5432</code> (Postgres on your project instance)</li>
<li>Dedicated pooler, transaction mode: <code>6543</code> (PgBouncer on your project instance)</li>
<li>Shared pooler, transaction mode: <code>6543</code> (Supavisor, multi-tenant)</li>
<li>Shared pooler, session mode: <code>5432</code> (Supavisor, multi-tenant)</li>
</ul>
<p>The port helps route the connection to the right pooler/mode.</p>
<h3 id="does-connection-pooling-affect-latency" class="group scroll-mt-24">Does connection pooling affect latency?<a href="#does-connection-pooling-affect-latency" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p>Because the dedicated pooler is hosted on the same machine as your database, it connects with lower latency than the shared pooler, which is hosted on a separate server. Direct connections have no pooler overhead but require IPv6 unless you have the IPv4 add-on.</p>
<h3 id="how-to-choose-the-right-connection-method" class="group scroll-mt-24">How to choose the right connection method?<a href="#how-to-choose-the-right-connection-method" class="ml-2 opacity-0 focus:opacity-100 group-hover:opacity-100 transition">#</a></h3>
<p><strong>Direct connection:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Best for: persistent backend services</li>
<li>Use for migrations, pg_dump, backup and management tools</li>
<li>Network: reachable over IPv6, or over IPv4 if the project has the <a href="/docs/guides/platform/ipv4-address" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">IPv4 add-on</a>.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Shared pooler (Supavisor):</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Best for: connections from IPv4 networks (IPv4-only on every tier)<!-- -->
<ul>
<li>Supavisor session mode → persistent backend on IPv4 networks</li>
<li>Supavisor transaction mode → serverless functions or short-lived tasks</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Use for application runtime traffic (queries, writes)</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Dedicated pooler (PgBouncer, paid tier):</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Best for: high-performance apps that need dedicated resources</li>
<li>Use for application runtime traffic (queries, writes)</li>
<li>Transaction mode only - use the Shared Pooler if you need session mode</li>
<li>Network: reachable over IPv6, or over IPv4 if the project has the <a href="/docs/guides/platform/ipv4-address" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">IPv4 add-on</a></li>
</ul>
<p>See the <a href="#how-to-connect-to-your-postgres-databases" class="underline transition underline-offset-2 decoration-inherit hover:decoration-foreground text-inherit hover:text-foreground">connection method matrix</a> at the top of this page for a quick reference, or follow the decision flow in the diagram below to choose the right option for your environment.</p>

For <strong>serverless or edge</strong> environments, use the dedicated pooler (PgBouncer, Pro plan) when IPv6 or the IPv4 add-on is available, or Supavisor in transaction mode when you need
